lines: The testament dative and Inventar of the goods geir soumes of money and debtis
perteining to umquhile William Glasgow in [locality obscured at gutter]

[giver-up and appointment formula; names/capacities partly illegible]

[confirmation formula naming] Alexr Broun and Jon Neilsone executoris datives
At Lanark the nynt day of Apryle 1673

plain_english: This is William Glasgow's Lanark Commissary Court testament dative and inventory. The ScotlandsPeople index confirms the indexed residence as Quodquen and the proceeding date as 9 April 1673; the manuscript locality and death wording remain obscured in the gutter.
Alexander Brown and John Neilson are repeatedly named as executors dative and personally appear to produce and swear the inventory.
William Neilson in Biggar is the cautioner or surety. A shared surname does not prove that he was related to John Neilson, and none of these offices proves kinship to William Glasgow.
No spouse, parent, child, or sibling is securely named in the supplied entry.
findings: Genuinely corrected reading: the first executor is Alexr (Alexander) Broun, not George Broun. The name repeats on images 25 and 26.
Confirmed: Jon Neilsone (John Neilson) is Alexander Brown's co-executor dative; both appear personally in the estate proceeding.
Confirmed: William Neilson in Biggar is cautioner, not a stated relative.
Unresolved: the opening locality, death month/year wording, names in the initial appointment formula, several account parties, and the presiding official's full name/title.
No direct kinship or new bridge to another Glasgow family is supplied by the testament.
changes_from_previous: Corrected every 'George Brown' conclusion to Alexander Brown from the repeated literal abbreviation 'Alexr Broun'.
Retained John Neilson as co-executor and William Neilson as cautioner; their administrative roles remain separate from family evidence.
Consolidated william-lanark-1673 as a duplicate alias rather than an independent case.
Preserved Glasgow-3912 as the maintained index-based identification while stating that Quothquan is not independently legible in the manuscript gutter.
